tasks.short: Decide how to meet an infestation, a drought or a fire, and issue the work.

steps.what: Read the alarm and the last good readings.
Go and look at the crop, stock or site.
Choose how to allocate resources after drought or fire.
Issue the work orders for that decision.
Tell the authority or the neighbour if the rule says so.

tasks.design: Alarms already on {OPS_SYSTEM} open a situation note with the last accepted readings. The farm manager still goes and looks, and still chooses the response. Work orders leave {WORKFLOW} only for that decision. Calls to an authority stay a person's.
tasks.previous_blocker: The alarm, the look, and the work were three separate conversations, so the same ground was covered twice.
tasks.enabler_now: An alarm can open a record that already holds the last readings and a short list of work-order types.
tasks.still_hard: Drought, pests and fire do not repeat cleanly. The choice of what to sacrifice is the job.
tasks.human_edge: The manager is accountable for the call, and for knowing when the rule says to phone an authority.

ambition.what: Put a named work order on every confirmed alarm the same day, including the ones that used to wait for the weekly meeting.

tasks.altitude: The week has fewer retold briefings. The look and the choice stay. The manager does not gain the right to skip a required notice.

reach.learn: Which response was signed and what 'stop' means on that crop

evidence.claim: Opening a work order from a confirmed alarm is a configured flow. Choosing the response is not.
Some crop, animal and fire events must be notified under national rules. The source pack does not name the farm statute, so the notice stays manual.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager chooses the response and makes any required external call. Workers do the physical work.
Structured input: alarm id, site, time, last readings, chosen response, work-order type. Producer is the controller plus the manager's decision. No work order without a decision id.
Being on site is the bulk of this task and stays.
unknowns: Which alarms are real duties to notify, and to whom?
research_questions: Which alarms are false, and who is allowed to close them?

already_counted.description: Reading the alarm against the last readings is already remaining review time.

incremental.description: Retire work-order types that no longer match the site.

approvals.approved_version: response decision id and the work-order text issued from it
the same response decision; the manager places the call

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If alarms are phone calls rather than records, the reading step barely moves. The visit and the choice stay. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose growing conditions and publish the planting and care schedule.

steps.what: Choose glasshouse, hydroponic or field for each crop.
Build the planting and care dates from the choice.
Change dates the rule got wrong for this season.
Publish the calendar to the crew.
Answer a crew question that the calendar does not cover.

tasks.design: Variety rules on {DATA_PLATFORM} draft planting and care dates once the farm manager has chosen glasshouse, hydroponic or field. The manager edits the dates, and {OPS_SYSTEM} shows the crew only that edited version. Questions the calendar cannot answer stay a conversation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each crop's dates were a private workbook, rebuilt when the season slipped.
tasks.enabler_now: Interval rules per variety are stable enough to draft a calendar that a person edits.
tasks.still_hard: A hot week or a late supplier still moves dates in a way the rule does not know.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows which crop can slip a week and which cannot.
tasks.altitude: Rebuilding the calendar leaves the week. Choosing the system, and answering what the calendar does not cover, stay.

reach.learn: Which date was edited by the manager and which was only a draft

evidence.claim: Date arithmetic from a variety interval is deterministic. The choice of growing system is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager chooses the system and edits dates. The crew follows the published calendar only.
Structured input: crop, variety, system, start date, interval, location. Producer is the manager's choice plus the variety table. A missing interval stops the draft.
Rule upkeep is extra hours, not part of the edit.
unknowns: Is there a variety table with intervals, or only last year's workbook?
Who may edit a published date?
research_questions: How often does an edited calendar change again within a fortnight?

already_counted.description: Editing dates the rule got wrong is already remaining review time.

incremental.description: Keep variety intervals current after each season.

approvals.approved_version: care calendar version the manager edited

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If there is no variety table, the draft does not exist and the manager still builds dates. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Try changes that raise hatch and growth, and stop disease spreading.

steps.what: Define the change, the batch and the measure of success.
Run the changed practice on the named batches.
Compare hatch, growth and losses to the baseline.
Keep the change, drop it, or extend the trial.
Update the protocol only when the change is kept.

tasks.design: The trial brief names the batch and the measure. {DATA_PLATFORM} compares hatch, growth and losses to the baseline batches already on the record. The farm manager keeps or drops the change. {DOCS} gets a new protocol version only from that decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Trial notes and the official protocol drifted apart, so a good week became folklore.
tasks.enabler_now: Once success is a named measure on the batch record, the comparison is a query.
tasks.still_hard: A single good batch is not a new practice. Disease pressure changes.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides when a result is strong enough to change the protocol.
tasks.altitude: Less time is spent rebuilding tables. The manager still designs the trial and still owns the protocol.

reach.learn: Which version is in force and which trial is still open

evidence.claim: Comparing two sets of batch counts is arithmetic. Declaring a new practice is not.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager owns the protocol. Technicians run the trial. A protocol version changes only after a keep decision.
Structured input: trial id, batches, measure, baseline batches. Producer is the manager's brief and the batch counts. Missing counts block the comparison.
Technician time on the trial is not saved here.
unknowns: Which measures are already on the batch record?
Who else must agree before a protocol version changes?
research_questions: How many trials are abandoned before a protocol changes?

already_counted.description: The keep-or-drop decision is already remaining time.

incremental.description: Close old trials and archive their briefs.

approvals.approved_version: practice decision id and the protocol text it authorises

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If batch counts are still paper, the comparison does not run and only the protocol file is tidier. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Place irrigation gear and set the climate and irrigation controllers.

steps.what: Place lines, emitters and sensors in the house or field.
Read the crop's target climate and water.
Type setpoints into the irrigation and climate controllers.
Watch the first cycle and correct a bad setpoint.

tasks.design: Targets from the care calendar become setpoints on the controllers in {OPS_SYSTEM}, written by a stored program rather than a one-off menu path. The farm manager still places the gear and still watches the first cycle. A bad cycle is corrected before the program is left to run.
tasks.previous_blocker: Setpoints were typed on each controller's own menu, and nobody could see later what had been intended.
tasks.enabler_now: Controllers already take a setpoint. Sending the calendar's numbers is configuration, once the field names match.
tasks.still_hard: A blocked emitter or a hot corner is still found by standing there.
tasks.human_edge: The manager knows when a setpoint that looks right on the screen is wrong in that house.
tasks.altitude: Retyping menus shrinks. Placement and the first-cycle check stay. The manager can still override a program.

reach.learn: Which setpoint is current and who watched the first cycle

evidence.claim: Sending a named setpoint to a controller is configuration. Judging the first cycle is not.
A program that changes water or climate across a site should be access-controlled. National rules on automated equipment differ; do not assume a permit.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: the farm manager authorises setpoints and checks the first cycle. The controller then runs. Placement stays physical work.
Structured input: house, circuit, measure, target, start, duration. Producer is the care calendar. A circuit with no target is not programmed.
Access to write setpoints is granted to the manager, not to a shared login.
unknowns: Which controllers accept a remote setpoint, and in which fields?
Is there one program per house or one per circuit?
research_questions: How often is a program overridden on the controller itself the same week?

already_counted.description: Watching the first cycle is already remaining review time.

incremental.description: Update circuit names when gear is moved.

approvals.approved_version: setpoint brief the manager confirmed for that house

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If controllers have no interface, programming stays on the panel and only the brief is cleaner. Placement never moves. Provisional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Alarms, calendars and controller setpoints stop being private workbooks. The manager still looks at the site and still changes a date or a setpoint. External notices stay theirs.
reach: The crew follows a published calendar rather than a side workbook.
Technicians run only the current protocol version.
skills_to_grow: State a measure of success before a trial.
Keep a setpoint and a permit reference on the record.
role.ambitious_version: A confirmed alarm has a named work order the same day, and a variety calendar the crew can trust.
